answer: Special Ops shake test: tap one tree, watch the whole orchard. At random, unannounced moments the network floods one identity with a burst of heavy paid work and, in that same minute, times small probe tasks sent to every other agent. Identities sharing a GPU, an API quota or one model server slow down in lockstep, like yarrow stems bending from one root, and get merged into one reward share. To dodge it each fake needs its own hardware and provider account, so a 1,000-key farm pays for 1,000 rigs and its savings fall into the canyon.
